title: HydroSheaf benchmarks: a harmonized identifiability comparison of directed connectivity, residence-time, and reaction inference in data-limited aquifers
scope: A companion benchmark article to M2.3 (the HydroSheaf framework paper). O3 does not introduce new software architecture. It harmonizes three already-locked, independently designed component benchmarks (M3 nuclear-tracer/age, M4 MODPATH-referenced topology, M5 PHREEQC-screened reaction) under one common identifiability taxonomy and reports a cross-component pattern that no single component paper can show on its own: under independent, prior-free evaluation, recall/sensitivity substantially exceeds precision/specificity in all three physically distinct inference problems, and apparent agreement improves only when a benchmark is recast as calibration/emulation against the same reference it is tested on.

objectives.statement: Harmonize the three components' independently designed benchmark protocols (reference type, positive/negative controls, independent-vs-prior-informed modes, reportability guards) into one common evidence taxonomy.
acceptance_criteria: A taxonomy table classifies every retained benchmark row from M3, M4 and M5 by independence, control type, and claim scope.
No benchmark row is re-labelled in a way that contradicts its component DECISIONS.md.

objectives.statement: Quantify, on a common recall/sensitivity versus precision/specificity axis, how each of the three inference layers performs when evaluated independently and without calibration to the reference it is judged against.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-component comparison figure and table report recall-type and precision-type metrics side by side for M3, M4 and M5 using each component's own locked headline metric.
Every reported value traces to a primary CSV/JSON artefact under M3/M4/M5 results/ or tables/ directories with no recomputation of the underlying inference.

objectives.statement: Quantify the screening-to-calibration/emulation gap that recurs in the age and reaction layers, and the independent-to-prior-informed gap that recurs in the topology layer, and state why calibrated or prior-informed numbers are not independent validation.
acceptance_criteria: Table reports both the independent/uncalibrated and the calibrated/prior-informed metric for each layer where both exist, with the non-independence stated in the same row.

objectives.statement: Compare the three benchmarks on computational and design scale (scenario count, fit count, runtime where recorded, external reference type) to give the reader a comp-geo-relevant sense of benchmark cost and reach.
acceptance_criteria: A benchmark-scale table reports scenario/fit counts and any recorded runtime for all three components from their own manifests.

objectives.statement: Describe, for a reader unfamiliar with the project, every dataset (synthetic and field) that any of the three benchmarks consumes, at a level sufficient to reproduce the comparison.
acceptance_criteria: Data section and a data-inventory table cover the USGS national groundwater-age release, the USGS Savage/Great Miami/Long Island MODFLOW-MODPATH archives, the 240-scenario PHREEQC factorial benchmark, and the Northern Ghana/Lower Anayari/Talensi field datasets, each with source, size, and role.

inputs.provenance: M3 locked age/TTD benchmark result tables (USGS national groundwater-age release comparison, TracerLPM strict-parity emulation, graph-regularization falsification test)
M4 locked topology benchmark result tables (USGS Savage/Great Miami/Long Island MODFLOW-MODPATH archives, independent vs MODPATH-informed graph modes)
M5 locked reaction benchmark result tables (240-scenario live-PHREEQC factorial inversion, conventional PHREEQC inverse baseline, Northern Ghana/Talensi/Lower Anayari field transfer)
M2.3 recomputed evidence exports, read only for cross-checking consistency with the companion framework paper, not as a primary evidence source for O3

risks.risk: Overlap/self-plagiarism against M2.3, which already reports a compressed version of the same three-way pattern.
risks.mitigation: O3 is explicitly framed as the depth companion to M2.3's compressed treatment; Discussion states the relationship and non-duplication explicitly; O3 reports full benchmark design, ablations and computational cost that M2.3's 7,000-word budget excludes.

risks.risk: M3/M4/M5 locked results predate the 2026-08-01/02 hydrosheaf/validation programme-layer changes.
risks.mitigation: Verified those commits touch the RUN-INTEGRATION-FULL programme/decision-utility layer used by M2.3's integrated claim, not the core nuclear/, sheaf/topology_refine.py inference paths M3/M4 benchmark, nor the reactions.py dictionary M5 benchmarks against; M2.3 itself reused M3's pre-Aug-1 results without rerunning them. Any residual staleness risk is disclosed in Limitations rather than silently assumed away.

risks.risk: Re-deriving cross-component numbers could silently diverge from each component's own locked, reviewed values.
risks.mitigation: Python synthesis layer reads only already-locked CSV/JSON artefacts and performs no re-simulation; every derived number is cross-checked against the value quoted in the component's own docs/*_results_summary.md.
